Definition: from G809; an indecency; by implication, the pudenda:--shame, that which is unseemly.
BiblicalUsage: Shame here is the nakedness that ought to be covered, and it is used twice. Paul says men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves the recompence of their error; and John says blessed is he that watcheth and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for shameful nakedness carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning, that sin strips a man bare, and the blessing is on the one who keeps his garments.
